body: The backend platform of Dragonfly: HTTP APIs, databases with relations, migrations and transactions, events, AI agents and graphs, written once in Nuclear and built with either dialect: `fastapi` (Python: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, LangGraph) or `nestjs` (TypeScript: NestJS, Sequelize, LangChain.js).
This repository is a folder of the NuclearLang working tree (`nuclear/dragonfly-backend`); the platform's rules are the
working tree's `../AGENTS.md` ([nuclear](https://github.com/nuclearlang/nuclear/blob/main/AGENTS.md)) and its state is `../STATUS.md`.
- Context of this repository: [docs/context/dragonfly-backend/CONTEXT.md](docs/context/dragonfly-backend/CONTEXT.md).

- What is inside: `dialects/backend/` (the platform contract, `fastapi`, `nestjs`), `packages/{dragonfly-py,dragonfly-nest}` (the runtimes), `defs/{python,typescript}/`, `spec/{backend,fastapi,nestjs}.md`, `examples/` (`tasks_api` builds with both dialects), `tools/{fastapi,nestjs}-check`, `docs/`.
- Checks:
```sh
(cd .. && cargo test)                 # the examples with both dialects, the goldens
sh tools/fastapi-check/check.sh       # pyright --strict, pytest, migrations, a live run
sh tools/nestjs-check/check.sh        # tsc --strict, node:test, migrations, a live run

rows.body: All notable changes to dragonfly-backend are written here; versions follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org).

rows.title: Changelog — Unreleased
rows.summary: Unreleased
body: - First public version.
- HTTP repositories (`Http` connection, bodiless `@get`/`@post`...) in fastapi and nestjs; `@key` for a JSON key that differs from the field; `[[generators]]` for `dragonfly gen` (ADR-0103).
- `[[generators.usecase]]`: `dragonfly gen usecase` writes a use case over a repository method, its alias in the facade and its route (ADR-0103).

- The order of a controller's routes no longer matters, in both dialects: a fixed segment wins over a parameter. Before, fastapi added the routes by method name (`GET <prefix>/search` of a generated resource answered 400, taken by `{id}`) and nestjs in the order written (`dragonfly-py` `router_of`, `dragonfly-nest` `configureApp`; `spec/backend.md` §2.7).
- `[[generators.resource]]`: the repository and the controller are merged (`merge = true`), so an action added to a resource that exists gets the members it lacks (ADR-0105).

- nestjs: `npm test` (what `dragonfly test` runs) removes `dist/test` before compiling: `tsc` never deletes the output of a source that is gone, so a test that was deleted or renamed kept running from its old `.js` and failed the project.

rows.title: Dragonfly for backend — the platform and its dialects `fastapi` and `nestjs`
rows.summary: Future repository `dragonfly-backend` (ADR-0093 amends ADR-0083).
body: Future repository `dragonfly-backend` (ADR-0093 amends ADR-0083). Decisions: ADR-0093 (platforms), ADR-0089 (python
dialect), ADR-0090 (Python backend), ADR-0091 (NestJS backend), ADR-0092 (plugins), ADR-0100 (data: `@primary(generated)`,
TypeORM relations, `relations(...)`, `paginate` → `Page<T>`, `@transactional`).
**The platform** (`spec/backend.md`, Nuclear only): components with `data/` (entities, repositories), `domain/`
(models, use cases), `api/` (controllers), `ai/` (tools, agents, states, graphs), `events/` (listeners) and the
`appcomponent` facade; `config/project_config.nuc` with the connections; `config.nuc` with `dragonfly(platform =
"backend", dialect = ...)`, `app(...)` and `plugins(...)`; tests in `test/*_test.nuc`; errors as `Result`; the
standard library of Nuclear (`spec/library.md`). The same `.nuc` builds with every dialect below; the conformance
test (ADR-0093 §9) builds one example with both. Contract file: `dialects/backend/platform.toml` (phase B1).

rows.title: Dragonfly for backend — the platform and its dialects `fastapi` and `nestjs` — Runtimes
rows.summary: `[decorators.args]` and `[decorators.fields]` of `dialects/backend/platform.toml` (merged into both dialects by the loader; the emitter's `check_field_rules` raises N0308 with no decorator name in Rust, comparing Nuclear names so fastapi's snake_case output does not matter).
body: **Data (ADR-0100), how it is built.** The rules of the relation decorators are data of the platform:
`[decorators.args]` and `[decorators.fields]` of `dialects/backend/platform.toml` (merged into both dialects by the
loader; the emitter's `check_field_rules` raises N0308 with no decorator name in Rust, comparing Nuclear names so
fastapi's snake_case output does not matter). Templates read `tinfo.decor` (the related entity's table),
`tinfo.fields_decor.primary` (its key), `owner` / `owner_decor` (the entity the field is in) and `|unquote`.
- fastapi: `many_to_one` / `one_to_many` / `many_to_many` / `one_to_one` in `orm.py` (`lazy="raise"`; the foreign key
is appended to the table in `Entity.__init_subclass__`; join tables are made when the mappers are configured, so
`Database.open` calls `configure_mappers()` and SQLite runs `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`); `to_dict` and `EntitySchema`
leave unloaded relations out; two entities import each other only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` (`[kinds.entity]
type_imports = true` + the python dialect's `[syntax] type_imports`); `main.py` and `conftest.py` list every entity
(`entities=[...]`) so SQLAlchemy knows all tables. Transactions: a `ContextVar` session that `Repository.use()` joins.
- nestjs: the runtime's `Entity` base keeps the relations given to the constructor (sequelize drops them), `save`

rows.title: Contracts: one backend, its apps generated — 1. The backend publishes its contract
rows.summary: Nothing to write.
body: Nothing to write. Building the backend (`nuclear build .`, `dragonfly build`, or the editor when it checks the
project) writes two files next to the project card:
| File | Holds |

| `.nuclear/contract.json` | the controllers and their routes (verb, path, parameters and where each goes, body, answer, error, status), the models those carry (fields, Nuclear types, defaults, JSON names, validation rules, the key field, doc comments) |
| `.nuclear/openapi.json` | the same as OpenAPI 3.1, for Swagger UI, generators or an HTTP tool |
Both are copied into `build/` and the running API serves them at `GET /.nuclear/contract.json` and
`GET /.nuclear/openapi.json`. The contract is the same whether the backend is built with `fastapi` or `nestjs`.
```nuclear
// tasks_api/components/tasks/api/tasks_controller.nuc
// The CRUD of tasks.
@controller("tasks")
controller TasksController(tasks: TasksAppComponent)
@get("{id}")
one(id: int) Result<Error, Task>
~tasks.task(id)
@post()
create(input: NewTask) Result<Error, Task>
~tasks.create(input)

connections: Connection[] = [
Http(connectionName = "tasks_api", baseUrl = "http://localhost:3000/"),
**Not a monorepo?** Point at the running API instead and fetch the contract when you want to follow a change:
```nuclear
contracts(tasks_api = "https://api.example.com")
```sh
nuclear contracts update          # GET https://api.example.com/.nuclear/contract.json → contracts/tasks_api/
nuclear contracts list            # each contract, its source, the version of the copy
The copy (`contracts/tasks_api/contract.json`) is committed with the app: a build never needs the network, and the
diff of a commit shows exactly what changed in the API.

rows.title: Contracts: one backend, its apps generated — 3. What the build generates
rows.summary: `contracts/tasks_api/` is written at every build (a path) or by `contracts update` (a url); the files say they are generated.
body: `contracts/tasks_api/` is written at every build (a path) or by `contracts update` (a url); the files say they
are generated. The mobile example `examples/examples-flutter-dialect/tasks_app` gets:
```nuclear
// contracts/tasks_api/models/task.nuc
Task
@primary
id: int
title: string
done: boolean = false
// 1 high, 2 normal, 3 low
priority: int = 2
createdAt?: DateTime
// contracts/tasks_api/models/new_task.nuc
NewTask
@maxLength(200)
@minLength(1)
title: string
@max(3)
@min(1)
priority: int = 2
// contracts/tasks_api/tasks_repository.nuc
@repository(path = "tasks", connection = "tasks_api")
repository TasksRepository
@get(local = true)
all(done?: boolean) Result<TasksApiError, Task[]>
@get(path = ":id", local = true)
one(id: int) Result<TasksApiError, Task>
@post
create(input: NewTask) Result<TasksApiError, Task>
The rules of `NewTask` came from the backend: a form on it refuses what the API refuses. `Task` has its key, so
the GETs get `local = true` and `allAsLocal()` / `oneAsLocal()` answer offline. Only what the app's platform
understands is written (a web app gets no `@primary` and no rules until it has forms and a local database).

rows.title: Contracts: one backend, its apps generated
rows.summary: A backend written in Nuclear describes its API once.
body: A backend written in Nuclear describes its API once. Every app that calls it (mobile, web) gets the models and
the repositories **generated from that description** instead of writing them by hand, and a change in the API is
caught when the app builds, not on the phone (ADR-0098). Backend and app stay two projects, deployed apart, talking
over HTTP: what travels is a JSON description, as OpenAPI or a `.proto` file would.
